data.title: Report C: where an in-repo work journal adds something an agent cannot already get, and where it adds nothing
body: # Report C: where an in-repo work journal adds something an agent cannot already get, and where it adds nothing

- **Date:** 2026-09-18 · **Method:** desk research. Vendor docs, changelogs and papers, all fetched on 2026-09-18. Two local checks were run in the FlowIt repository (`src/core/git.ts`; `kadence prime` output size).

- **Scope:** this report contains only evidence that is new, or that corrects something in `discovery-verdict`, `context-handoff`, `agent-readability`, `competitive-snapshot`, `feature-gap`, `probe-c` and `strategy`. It does not repeat anything those documents already say.
- **Labels:** **Fact** means a primary source says it or it was measured. **Inference** is our reading of the facts. **Assumption** is load-bearing and has no evidence behind it.
- **Stance:** adversarial. Every section asks where kadence is redundant before it asks where kadence helps.
## 0. Verdict first

1. **The premise that "no platform shares agent state between different humans" is no longer true.** It holds only when you add "across vendors, and in git". The vendors share state inside their own walls:
- GitHub Copilot Memory is repository-scoped and shared with every user who has read access.
- Amp threads are shared across a workspace.
- Cursor Projects sync their context files across machines.
- Claude Code has a documented, git-versioned subagent memory scope (`.claude/agent-memory/`). It also has an undocumented server-synced "team memory" in its code.
Two gaps remain real:
- **(a) State that more than one vendor can read, versioned with the code, restored by `git checkout`.**
- **(b) Structure: tasks, claims, and decisions with rejected alternatives.** None of the vendor memories store these; they all store free-text "facts".
2. **Strongest new evidence FOR the category.** Two results:
- GitHub's A/B test of repository-shared memory: PR merge rate rose from 83% to 90% (p < 0.00001).
- DreamBench-SWE: facts from earlier sessions that the agent could not work out from the code took pass rates from about 12% without memory to 46–54% with it.
Neither result is about kadence, and both measure memory the system wrote *automatically*.
3. **Strongest new evidence AGAINST kadence's current shape.** Three results:
- Context loaded into every session beat context the agent had to decide to fetch: 100% vs 53–79%. With default behaviour, the skill was not invoked in 56% of cases.
- Instruction compliance decays inside a session, by about 5.6% lower odds per generated function.
- For the most common parallel-agent setup (worktrees on one machine), kadence claims are invisible between worktrees. Claude's native task list and file lock already cover that setup.

4. **Redundant, with value of zero or close to it:** a checklist for one agent on one machine; free-text memory for one person; sharing inside a single vendor; locking on one machine; anything the agent can derive from the code or the git log.
## 1. What the platforms provide natively (September 2026)
### 1.1 Claude Code
| Mechanism | Scope, and whether it is shared | Source (fetched 2026-09-18) |

| Auto memory, `MEMORY.md` (first 200 lines / 25 KB loaded) | "machine-local … Files are not shared across machines or cloud environments" | **Fact**. [memory docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) |

| **Subagent `memory: project`** at `.claude/agent-memory/<agent>/` | "shareable via version control"; **"`project` is the recommended default scope"**. `MEMORY.md` is loaded at 200 lines / 25 KB | **Fact**. [sub-agents docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents); listed as committed in [.claude directory docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory) |

| **Team memory sync** at `~/.claude/projects/<hash>/memory/team/`, keyed by `owner/repo` | Synced through Anthropic servers, with server-wins pull and ETag-based optimistic concurrency. **Undocumented**; found in leaked npm source maps on 2026-03-31. Claude-only; needs first-party OAuth | **Fact** that it exists in code, per a secondary source dated 2026-04-05 ([Goldsborough](https://jakegoldsborough.com/blog/2026/inside-claude-codes-team-memory-sync/)). Not in the official memory docs as of 2026-09-18. **Inference:** it may ship |
| Shared team memory feature request | #38536, open since 2026-03-25, no maintainer reply | **Fact**. [issue #38536](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/38536) |

| Tasks (`TaskCreate`/`TaskList`…), shared through `CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID` → `~/.claude/tasks/<id>/` | Same machine only. **Default only on Claude 3.x, Opus 4–4.7, Sonnet 4–4.6, Haiku 4.5.** Off on newer models (Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Fable) because "Claude keeps track of multi-step work without a written checklist, and the tools' definitions and reminders take up context". Opt-in with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` | **Fact**. [interactive mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode), [tools reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference) |

| Agent teams (experimental; `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`) | Shared task list with dependencies; "Task claiming uses **file locking**". Stored under `~/.claude/tasks/{team}` and "never uploaded". Limits: "One team per session"; "Task status can lag"; "Avoid file conflicts… Two teammates editing the same file leads to overwrites" | **Fact**. [agent teams](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams), described as of v2.1.178 |

| Cross-session messaging | The user's *own* sessions, across machines through Remote Control. Explicitly aimed at "Coordinate parallel worktrees". Plain text only, not persisted as a journal | **Fact**. [cross-session messaging](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging), v2.1.224+ |

| SessionStart hook | Plain-text stdout is added "as context that Claude can see and act on". Matchers: `startup/resume/clear/compact/fork` | **Fact**. [hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) |

| `/import` of `AGENTS.md` | One-time copy of `AGENTS.md` into `CLAUDE.md` (v2.1.213+). Claude Code still "reads `CLAUDE.md`, not `AGENTS.md`" | **Fact**. [memory docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) |
### 1.2 Other vendors
| Vendor | Cross-session state | Shared across humans? | In git? | Source (fetched 2026-09-18) |

| **GitHub Copilot** | **Copilot Memory**: repository-scoped facts with code citations, verified "just in time" against the current code, "automatically deleted after 28 days" if unused. Used by the cloud agent, code review and CLI. Public preview; on by default for individual plans; an admin must enable it for org and enterprise plans | **Yes.** Repository facts are "available to any user who has access to Copilot Memory in that repository"; memories can only be created from actions by contributors with write permission | No, stored in GitHub's service | **Fact**. [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-memory); [GitHub blog 2026-01-15](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/building-an-agentic-memory-system-for-github-copilot/); [changelog 2026-03-04](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-03-04-copilot-memory-now-on-by-default-for-pro-and-pro-users-in-public-preview/) |

| **Cursor** | Memories (GA). **Projects** (beta, 2026-09-10): a coordinator agent plus files that "sync across every cloud and local machine its agents use". "It isn't available on Enterprise plans" | Storage location and team visibility **undocumented** | Not stated | **Fact**. [Projects blog 2026-09-10](https://cursor.com/blog/projects), [Projects docs](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/projects) |

| **OpenAI Codex** | Memories in `~/.codex/memories/`, generated in the background from idle chats; "Local Codex memories are **off by default**" | No, local | No | **Fact**. [learn.chatgpt.com memories](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/customization/memories?surface=app) |

| **Amp** | Threads; `/handoff` generates a prompt and file list for a new thread (2025-10-23); Amp can read other threads | **Yes**, inside a workspace: threads "shared by default with your workspace members" | No | **Fact**. [handoff](https://ampcode.com/news/handoff); [manual](https://ampcode.com/manual); [end of public threads](https://ampcode.com/news/end-of-public-threads) |

| **Gemini CLI** | `save_memory` writes to `GEMINI.md`, and routes shared project facts to the repository `GEMINI.md`. Task Tracker is experimental (`experimental.taskTracker`) | Only through a committed `GEMINI.md` | Only if committed | **Fact**. [memory tool docs](https://geminicli.com/docs/tools/memory/); [v0.40.0 notes](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/discussions/26216) |

| **Claude API** | Memory tool: the client implements the storage, so it is a primitive, not a store. Memory + context editing gave "+39% over baseline"; context editing alone +29%; −84% tokens on a 100-turn web-search eval | Whatever the developer builds | Whatever the developer builds | **Fact**. [context management, 2025-09-29](https://claude.com/blog/context-management); [memory tool docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool) |
### 1.3 Hooks: `prime` is now deliverable to five vendors, not one
| Vendor | SessionStart context injection | Source (fetched 2026-09-18) |
| Claude Code | Yes (stdout or `additionalContext`) | [hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) |

| Codex | Yes. "Plain text on `stdout` is added as extra developer context". Hooks first shipped in v0.114 (March 2026, per a secondary source). Open bug: the hook does not fire when a thread is auto-restored ([#24228](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/24228)) | [learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks) |
| Cursor | Yes: `additional_context` in `<project-root>/.cursor/hooks.json`. **Not available in cloud agents** | [Cursor hooks](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks) |

| Copilot (cloud agent, CLI) | Yes: "can inject `additionalContext` into the session". `.github/hooks/*.json` must be on the default branch for the cloud agent | [hooks reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference); [about hooks](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/hooks) |
| Gemini CLI | Yes. Interactive: "Injected as the first turn in history"; non-interactive: prepended to the prompt | [hooks reference](https://geminicli.com/docs/hooks/reference/) |
**Fact (local check).** `kadence init --hooks` writes only `.claude/settings.json` (`src/cli/commands/init.ts`). In the FlowIt repository `prime` is **1,232 bytes, about 350 tokens**.
### 1.4 What this confirms and what it refutes
- **Refuted:** "a teammate cloning the repo gets none of it" (competitive-snapshot §2) and "CC Tasks/Memory ❌ Claude only, machine-local" (feature-gap).
- Claude Code documents git-shared subagent memory and recommends it as the default scope.
- Copilot shares repository memory across humans, and it is the only vendor to have published an A/B result.
**Fact.**

- **Confirmed:** no native mechanism is **readable by more than one vendor** and **versioned with the code**. Every shared store is either a vendor service (Copilot, Amp, Cursor Projects, Claude team memory) or a git file that only one vendor reads (`.claude/agent-memory/`). `AGENTS.md` crosses vendors, but it is instructions, not state. **Fact** (absence across the docs above) and **Inference** (that nothing was missed).

- **Confirmed:** no vendor memory stores **tasks, claims or decisions with rejected alternatives** as structured records. All of them store free-text facts, preferences or conversation threads. **Fact.**

- **New risk:** the "cross-human" gap is closing *inside* each vendor. For a team on only Copilot, or only Amp, or (once team memory ships) only Claude, the vendor answer costs nothing to install. **Inference.**
## 2. How agents use tools: what is new since Probe C and the agent-readability doc
1. **Context loaded into every session beats context the agent has to fetch.**

- **Fact.** Vercel (2026-01-27), on Next.js tasks: no docs 53%; skill 53% (**not invoked in 56% of cases**); skill with an explicit "use it" instruction 79%; an 8 KB compressed docs index in `AGENTS.md` **100%**. The authors' stated reason: loading the index up front removes the decision point from the agent ([Vercel](https://vercel.com/blog/agents-md-outperforms-skills-in-our-agent-evals)).

- **Inference.** kadence's CLI, `task show`, `decision list` and the planned skill package (strategy C6) all depend on the agent *deciding* to call them. The SessionStart `prime` is the only part of kadence that reaches the agent without that decision. The context-handoff doc (§5 #3) said "do not build delegated/automated layers". That position is obsolete: the hook is exactly that layer, and it is the one part with evidence behind it.
2. **Tool search and deferred loading shrink the MCP cost that Probe C measured.**

- **Fact.** Tool Search cut an initial load of about 77K tokens to about 8.7K (−85%), and accuracy rose (Opus 4: 49→74%; Opus 4.5: 79.5→88.1%). Tool-use examples raised complex-parameter accuracy from 72% to 90% ([Anthropic, 2025-11-24](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use)).
- **Fact.** Code execution with MCP cut one workflow from 150,000 tokens to 2,000 (−98.7%) ([Anthropic, 2025-11-04](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp)).

- **Fact.** Claude Code defers MCP tools by default on supported models, so a server connecting "only appends new content and doesn't disturb anything already cached" ([Claude Code prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching)).

- **Inference.** Probe C's roughly 700 tokens per session for an MCP wrapper is now nearer 0 upfront on Claude Code. The MCP-vs-CLI cost argument is dead in both directions. What actually decides the matter is discovery (the agent knows kadence exists) and zero install.
3. **The shape of the output matters, and one kadence decision is validated.**

- **Fact.** "Agents also tend to grapple with natural language names, terms, or identifiers significantly more successfully than they do with cryptic identifiers". Replacing UUIDs with meaningful names "significantly improves Claude's precision in retrieval tasks by reducing hallucinations".

- **Fact.** In the same article: a concise response format used about ⅓ of the tokens of a detailed one (72 vs 206), and "For Claude Code, we restrict tool responses to 25,000 tokens by default" ([Anthropic, 2025-09-11](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents)).

- **Inference.** Showing `KAD-N`/`DEC-N` labels and hiding ULIDs is the recommended pattern. The 25k cap is a second reason for `--fields`/`--summary`: at 1000 tasks, `board --json` (803 KB) would be truncated by the harness.
4. **JSON state is harder for the model to corrupt, and plain files get most of the way.**

- **Fact.** "The model is less likely to inappropriately change or overwrite JSON files compared to Markdown files" ([Anthropic, 2025-11-26](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents)).

- **Fact.** Anthropic's current prompting guide says: "Use structured formats for state data", "Use git for state tracking", and "Claude's latest models are extremely effective at discovering state from the local filesystem" ([prompting best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices)).

- **Inference, adversarial.** This supports the *shape* (JSON events in git). It also means a plain `progress.json` plus `git log` gets a single agent most of the benefit, with no tool at all. kadence's increment over that is **merge semantics for more than one writer**, not the structure.
5. **Adherence to `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`: what is now measured.**
- **Fact.** ETH (arXiv 2602.11988, 2026-02-12), across four agents on SWE-bench Lite plus 138 tasks:
- Context files "do not generally improve task success rates, while increasing inference cost by over 20% on average".
- LLM-generated files gave about −3% and developer-written files about +4%; neither is significant.
- "Repository overviews … are not helpful" ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11988)).

- **Fact.** arXiv 2601.20404 (2026-01-28), 10 repositories, 124 PRs: with `AGENTS.md`, median runtime fell 28.64% and output tokens fell 16.58%, with task completion comparable ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20404)).
- **Fact.** McMillan (arXiv 2605.10039, 2026-05-11), 1,650 Claude Code sessions and 16,050 function-level observations:

- File size, instruction position, file architecture and conflicting adjacent files showed **no detectable effect** on compliance. Size and conflict nulls are backed by affirmative Bayes factors (BF10 0.05–0.10).
- The largest effect is **within the session**: odds of compliance fall about 5.6% per generated function (OR 0.944, non-monotonic) ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10039)).
- **Fact.** IFScale (arXiv 2507.11538, 2025-07-15): at 500 simultaneous instructions the best model reached 68%, with a bias toward earlier instructions ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.11538)).

- **Fact.** Claude Code's own docs: CLAUDE.md "is delivered as a user message after the system prompt… there's no guarantee of strict compliance". For must-run behaviour, "write it as a hook instead" ([memory docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory)).
- **Corrections and inference:**
- The "~150–200 instructions / ~300 lines ceiling" in agent-readability §2 is contradicted for single instructions by the only controlled study found.
- The real risk to kadence is **decay across a session**: "write a decision or note when you choose" is read at minute 0 and needed at minute 40.
- The ETH result warns that injected context is a cost of +20% unless its content is something the agent could not work out from the code.
## 3. Context rot, `prime` size, position, and caching

- **Fact.** Chroma (2025-07-14, 18 models incl. Claude 4, GPT-4.1, Gemini 2.5, Qwen3): performance "grows increasingly unreliable as input length grows", even on trivial tasks. **Even a single distractor reduced performance.** Logically structured haystacks did worse than shuffled ones. LongMemEval focused prompts (~300 tokens) clearly beat full prompts (~113k) ([Chroma](https://www.trychroma.com/research/context-rot)).

- **Inference.** At about 350 tokens, `prime` is too small for length-driven rot to matter. The live risk is **distractors**. The "Decisions in force" and "Recent notes" lines are not filtered to the task at hand, and `prime` cannot know the task at session start. DreamBench (§4) measured the same failure: irrelevant imports in 47% of retrieved memories, over-scoped facts in 17%. Separately, the local check shows decision titles truncated mid-word ("…reposito…").

- **Fact.** Claude Code orders a request as: system prompt → project context (`CLAUDE.md`, auto memory, unscoped rules) → conversation. SessionStart hook output enters as context at the start of the conversation. The prompt cache is "effectively scoped to one machine and directory". Sequential sessions share a prefix "only when the git status snapshot taken at startup matches". Editing CLAUDE.md mid-session neither applies nor breaks the cache ([Claude Code prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching)).

- **Inference, a correction to a likely worry.** Non-deterministic `prime` output (new events, relative times) **does not cost cache hits in practice**. Claude Code's prefix already changes every session with the git status snapshot, and the hook runs once per session start, clear or compaction, so the block is stable inside a session. Put it in `CLAUDE.md` via `@import` of a generated file and the result is the same. What *would* break the cache: rewriting `prime` mid-session through a per-turn hook such as `UserPromptSubmit`, or changing tool definitions. Rule: **inject once per session, never per turn.**

- **Fact.** API caching rules: prefix order is tools → system → messages, and a change at any level invalidates that level and everything after it. The 5-minute TTL is the default, and 1-hour writes cost 2× base input. Cache reads cost 0.1×. The minimum cacheable prefix is 512 tokens on Opus 5 / Fable and 1,024 on Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8. There are at most 4 breakpoints, with a 20-block lookback ([API prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching)). None of this bears on a block of about 350 tokens that sits inside a larger prefix.
## 4. Does persistent structured state improve outcomes? The measured evidence
| Study | What was persisted | Result | Label |

| GitHub Copilot Memory A/B ([2026-01-15](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/building-an-agentic-memory-system-for-github-copilot/)) | Repository-shared facts with code citations, verified before use | Coding agent PR merge rate **90% vs 83%**; code-review positive feedback 77% vs 75%; p < 0.00001; code-review precision +3%, recall +4% | Fact (vendor-reported, not independent) |

| DreamBench-SWE ([arXiv 2608.20664](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20664), 2026-08-21), Codex CLI / gpt-5.5, 60 traps × 3 seeds | Facts from earlier sessions that the agent could not work out from the code: reviewer conventions, superseded architecture facts, generated-file boundaries, flaky-test lessons | v2.1 successor audit: no memory **11.67%**; deterministic verbatim event memory **45.56%**; typed + raw reference 46.11%; hosted Mem0 53.89%. The original fold was null on its primary contrast (95/180 vs 89/180, p = .518). Aggregate diagnostics: **StaleUseRate 0.20**, IrrelevantImportRate 0.47, OverscopeRate 0.17 | Fact. The authors themselves caution against claiming one mechanism beats another; the HTML version reports other per-fold numbers |

| Letta ([2025-08-12](https://www.letta.com/blog/benchmarking-ai-agent-memory)) | Plain files + filesystem tools vs specialised memory | Filesystem agent (GPT-4o mini) 74.0% on LoCoMo vs Mem0's reported 68.5% | Fact |
| Anthropic memory + context editing ([2025-09-29](https://claude.com/blog/context-management)) | Client-side memory files | +39% over baseline; −84% tokens | Fact (vendor) |
| ETH AGENTS.md ([2602.11988](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11988), 2026-02-12) | Static context files | No significant success gain; +20% cost | Fact |
| AGENTS.md efficiency ([2601.20404](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20404), 2026-01-28) | Static context file | −28.64% runtime, −16.58% output tokens | Fact |

| Anthropic long-running harness ([2025-11-26](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents)) | `feature_list.json` + `claude-progress.txt` + git + `init.sh` | Qualitative only, **no numbers published**. Named failure modes without it: one-shotting, declaring victory early, a new session not knowing prior work | Fact |

| SlopCodeBench ([2603.24755](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24755)) | None; the agent iteratively extends its own code | Erosion in 77% of trajectories, verbosity in 75.5%. Best agent passed 14.8% of checkpoints. Quality guidance cut the *level* of degradation by up to a third but not its rate | Fact |

| Microsoft rollout ([2607.01418](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01418), 2026-07-01) | Not about memory. Adoption of Claude Code and Copilot CLI | Adopters merged about 24% more PRs; first use spread "primarily through social networks" | Fact (context for how adoption spreads) |
**Inference.**
- The measured wins come from **facts the agent could not work out itself, relevant to the task**, that reach the agent **without the agent asking**.
- The measured failures come from **stale, over-scoped and irrelevant** memory.
- Nothing measures a *structured work journal* specifically, and nothing measures *cross-vendor* handoff. kadence's claim of value in those two areas remains **Assumption**.

**The second-strongest caveat.** Every positive result above comes from **automatic capture**: Copilot writes its memories itself; DreamBench writes one memory per trajectory. kadence depends on explicit writes, and adherence to instructions decays within a session (§2.5). This is feature-gap G-1 with evidence behind it now. **Inference.**
### Metrics kadence can reuse to measure its own value
| Metric | From | How kadence would use it |

| **Repeated-rejected-path rate**: opportunities where a later session re-attempts an approach recorded as `--rejected` | DreamBench RepeatedErrorRate | Core metric for "decisions with rejected alternatives" |
| **StaleUseRate**: a superseded decision still applied | DreamBench | Tests `--supersedes` |
| **Useful-context precision**: `prime` lines the agent actually used ÷ lines injected | DreamBench UsefulMemoryPrecision / IrrelevantImportRate | Sizes and filters `prime` |
| Task success **and** token cost, with vs without | ETH 2602.11988 | Guards against the +20% cost trap |
| Runtime and output tokens per PR | arXiv 2601.20404 | Cheap proxy |
| PR merge rate, A/B | GitHub Copilot Memory | Pilot-level outcome, if a pilot has the volume |
| Joint success of 2 agents vs solo; duplicated-work rate | CooperBench; MAST "step repetition" 17.14% | Tests claims |
| Write-back compliance per session step | McMillan 2605.10039 (OR per step) | Tests whether agents write `note`/`decision` without being pushed (strategy N2) |
## 5. Multi-agent coordination: failure modes and how others solve them

- **Fact.** CooperBench ([arXiv 2601.13295](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13295), 2026-01-19): across 600+ tasks in 12 libraries, two agents on separable features score **about 30% lower together than when each works alone** ("curse of coordination"). Failure causes: expectation 42%, commitment 32%, communication 26% ([blog](https://cooperbench.com/blog/curse-of-coordination)).

- **Fact.** MAST ([arXiv 2503.13657](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.13657), NeurIPS 2025), 1,600+ traces across 7 frameworks: specification 41.77%, inter-agent misalignment 36.94%, verification 21.30%. The most common single mode is **step repetition, 17.14%**.

- **Fact.** Anthropic's multi-agent research system (2025-06-13): 90.2% better than single-agent Opus 4 on its internal research eval, at about 15× the tokens of chat. Token usage explains 80% of the variance in results. Early versions had subagents duplicating work under vague task descriptions. The lead agent saves its plan to memory because context above 200k tokens is truncated ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)).

- **Fact.** Cognition: "Share context, and share full agent traces" and "Actions carry implicit decisions, and conflicting decisions carry bad results" ([Cognition](https://cognition.com/blog/dont-build-multi-agents)).

- **Fact.** Practitioner guides (2026): parallel agents in worktrees duplicate each other's work "when branches can't see one another". Locks are advisory, so the real protection is decomposition. The recommended fix is a shared task document that every agent reads and marks ([MindStudio](https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/git-worktrees-parallel-ai-coding-agents); [Augment](https://www.augmentcode.com/guides/how-to-run-a-multi-agent-coding-workspace)). These are secondary sources.
- **How others solve claims:**
| System | Mechanism | Latency across agents |
| Claude agent teams | file lock, same machine | immediate |

| Beads v1.3.0 | lease with a 5-minute TTL, `heartbeat`, `reclaim --older-than`, `row_lock` compare-and-set, replica-aware leases over Dolt sync ([release notes](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/releases/tag/v1.3.0)) | a sync cycle |
| Claude cross-session messaging | plain-text notice between one user's sessions ([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging)) | immediate |
| kadence (ADR-011) | append-only claim event; `contested` appears after merge; no expiry | **push + pull + merge** |
**Fact.**
- **Fact (local check).** `findRepoRoot` uses `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, deliberately, so each git worktree has its own `.kadence/` (`src/core/git.ts`, lines 23–30).
**Inference, the sharpest technical finding here:**
- The commonest parallel-agent pattern of 2026 is N agents in N worktrees on one machine.

- In that pattern, a kadence claim in worktree A is **invisible** to the agent in worktree B until A's branch is committed and merged into B's. That is exactly the "branches can't see one another" duplication the guides describe.
- For this pattern the native answers are strictly better today: Claude task list with file lock, cross-session messaging, Beads leases.
- **Across humans on different machines**, kadence's append-and-merge is the honest ceiling without a network. It records contention; it does not prevent it.
## 6. Corrections to earlier documents
| Document | Claim | Correction | Evidence (fetched 2026-09-18) |

## 8. Technical bets: make or drop
1. **MAKE: install `prime` through every vendor's SessionStart hook, not only Claude's.**
- Codex `hooks.json`, Cursor `.cursor/hooks.json` (not cloud agents), Copilot `.github/hooks/*.json` (default branch), Gemini hooks in `settings.json`.
- Loading context into every session is the only delivery path with evidence behind it (100% vs 53–79%).
- Cross-vendor is the only gap nobody closes.
- Cost: file writes only, no network. It still needs asking first, because it is persistent configuration in the user's repository.
- Measure with the useful-context precision metric.

2. **MAKE: a write-back nudge at the end of the session.** Use a `Stop` hook in Claude, the Codex equivalent, or Copilot `sessionEnd`, installed only with `--hooks`. When the session touched a claimed task and wrote no `note`/`decision`, it prints one line asking the agent to record what was decided and rejected.
- Rationale: decay within the session (OR 0.944 per step), and every measured memory win comes from capture.
- This is G-1 in its smallest form. It needs no transcript capture, so the ADR constraints and privacy hold.
- Measure write-back compliance per session.
3. **MAKE: link decisions and notes to code, and flag staleness offline.**
- Add optional `--cites path[:line]` or a commit, and derive `stale: true` when cited files changed after the event (`git log -- path`, local).
- `prime` and `task show` hide or mark stale entries.
- This copies Copilot's just-in-time verification with no network and targets DreamBench's StaleUseRate.
- It is additive to `kadence/v1`, but it touches the `FlowEvent` shape, so it needs asking first under CLAUDE.md.
4. **MAKE or DROP, decided now: claims inside one machine.** Either:
- (a) read the `.kadence/events` of sibling worktrees (`git worktree list`, local, read-only) so `ready`/`claim` see same-machine claims before merge; or

- (b) stop presenting claims as coordination for parallel agents. Say instead "claims are a record for humans across machines; for parallel agents on one machine use your vendor's lock", and drop the fleet framing against Beads.
Leaving it as it is sells a guarantee that does not hold in the commonest setup.
5. **DROP: anything that duplicates single-agent or single-vendor memory.**
- Do not grow `prime` into a recall layer.
- Remove derivable content, such as recent notes that restate the git log. The ETH paper shows derivable context costs +20% for nothing, and Chroma shows that even one distractor hurts.
- Deprioritise the skill package (C6) as a *delivery* mechanism (56% non-invocation). Keep it only as a discovery listing.

- **Run a Probe D before 1.0** on the §4 metrics: session 1 records a decision with a rejected path; session 2 is a *different vendor*; conditions are none, `AGENTS.md` note, and kadence `prime`. Measure repeated-rejected-path rate and tokens. It is the cheapest way to turn "Assumption" into "Fact" for the one claim that is distinct.
